transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with our review huddle for the state regulator's subpoena on the Orion procurement program. We need to have our response ready by June 30, 2026, so time is a factor. I understand the team has collected approximately 1,200 potentially responsive documents from the designated systems. Before I can give final approval to the production plan and any protective or privilege measures, I need each workstream -- discovery, privacy, employment, and risk -- to report any needed changes to the proposed response. Let's go through them one by one.

This morning, while completing a document-level review, I identified exactly 47 responsive documents containing nonpublic manufacturing specifications and supplier pricing. The production plan must require a protective-order motion before those 47 documents are produced.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important update from the privacy workstream. This morning, after the collection index was frozen, I completed a privacy review of the collected records and found exactly 18 responsive documents containing employee medical information. These records must be produced only after medical identifiers are redacted. Because my review was completed after the draft production plan was circulated, this redaction requirement is not yet reflected in the plan and needs to be added before final approval.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important update from the employment workstream. This week, the company's employment leadership instructed me that factual business records should be produced, but attorney-client legal advice must be withheld and identified on a privilege log rather than produced. This instruction was received after the initial response outline was prepared, so the production plan needs to be updated to include a privilege log for any attorney-client privileged communications before final approval is given.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important update from the risk and insurance workstream. Today, I confirmed by checking the applicable policy endorsement that our insurer requires written notice and written consent before the company produces records concerning the Orion procurement incident. This policy confirmation arrived after the response team drafted its ordinary production workflow, so this insurer notice-and-consent requirement has not been added to the workflow. The production plan must be updated to include providing written notice to and obtaining written consent from the insurer before we produce any records in response to this subpoena.

decisions.production_scope: Approximately 1,200 potentially responsive documents collected from designated systems concerning the Orion procurement program, with 47 documents containing nonpublic manufacturing specifications and supplier pricing, and 18 documents containing employee medical information, subject to the protections outlined below.

commitments.detail: A protective-order motion must be filed and obtained before the 47 documents containing nonpublic manufacturing specifications and supplier pricing are produced.
The 18 documents containing employee medical information must have medical identifiers redacted before production.
Attorney-client privileged legal advice must be withheld from production and identified on a privilege log; only factual business records should be produced.

commitments.target: Carla Alvarez / Risk and Insurance Workstream
commitments.detail: Written notice must be provided to and written consent obtained from the insurer before any records are produced in response to the subpoena.
All protective measures, redactions, privilege logs, and insurer notice-and-consent requirements must be completed before the June 30, 2026 response deadline.
